  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Despite the success of discrete diffusion language models (dLMs) for fast parallel decoding, their non-smooth, high-dimensional space hinders trajectory steering for reasoning and inference acceleration. To overcome this, we present <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Nemotron-Labs-Sigma</span>, the first family of large-scale (3B/8B) continuous dLMs built on steerable, low-dimensional ODE/SDE latent trajectories. Trained blockwise via likelihood optimization, <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Nemotron-Labs-Sigma</span> jointly denoises Gaussian-corrupted token embeddings while learning an optimal embedding geometry, and leverages pretrained autoregressive (AR) weights for warm-starting. At inference, we identify classifier-free guidance and score temperature as essential for high-fidelity reasoning and coding. Against state-of-the-art discrete counterparts (masked dLMs and AR baselines), <span id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Nemotron-Labs-Sigma</span> outperforms them on standard benchmarks after pretraining (e.g., GSM8K, Minerva, HumanEval, MBPP) and on challenging reasoning tasks after supervised fine-tuning (e.g., MATH-500, AIME), with the largest consistent gains on coding. Beyond accuracy, we exploit two structural properties unique to continuous dLMs. First, smooth trajectories degrade gracefully at low NFEs and enable efficient few-step distillation: distribution matching proves strongest among the methods we study, giving roughly <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="8\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8\times</annotation></semantics></math> acceleration on math and <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times</annotation></semantics></math> on coding (<math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="abstract1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> tokens per forward pass) with negligible accuracy loss and preserved diversity. In addition, the one-step speculative decoding on the (pre-SFT) distilled 8B model yields a further <math id="abstract1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\sim\!3.5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∼</mo><mn>3.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim\!3.5\times</annotation></semantics></math> throughput gain over the AR counterpart (on GB200), outperforming masked dLM baselines. Second, embedding-space steering controls the quality–diversity trade-off, yielding strong pass@<math id="abstract1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> that keeps improving as <math id="abstract1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> grows. Together, these results establish continuous dLMs as a promising paradigm for efficient language generation. Model family weights are publicly available at <a href="https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/nemotron-labs-sigma" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href"><span class="ltx_text" style="position:relative; bottom:-1.1pt;"><img src="2610.02665v2/figures/hf-logo.png" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:14/14;" width="14" height="14" alt="[Uncaptioned image]"></span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Nemotron-Labs-Sigma</span></a>.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While diffusion language models (dLMs) enable fast parallel decoding compared to autoregressive (AR) baselines <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Inception Labs et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Song et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib84" title="" class="ltx_ref">DiffusionGemma Team et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, dominant discrete dLMs operate in high-dimensional, categorical state spaces (e.g., vocabulary size <math id="S1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V\geq 100\text{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>k</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V\geq 100\text{k}</annotation></semantics></math>) that suffer under limited step budgets and impede trajectory control for complex reasoning and coding tasks. Continuous diffusion offers a principled way to overcome these structural limitations through smooth latent geometries that natively support structured editing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Meng et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, flexible ODE trajectory steering <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang and Chen, 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lu et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib83" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, and efficient few-step distillation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Salimans and Ho, 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Song et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Recently, there has been growing interest in continuous diffusion and flow matching for text generation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gulrajani and Hashimoto, 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dieleman et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liang et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2026</a>)</cite>; see <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Related Work ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">App.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> for a review. However, existing methods remain limited in scale (<math id="S1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;2\text{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>B</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;2\text{B}</annotation></semantics></math> parameters) or focus on <span id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unconditional</span> generation, lacking evaluations on complex reasoning tasks. Whether continuous dLMs scale to complex conditional reasoning remains open. This is a non-trivial hurdle because continuous models update block embeddings globally, in contrast to the factorized categorical denoising of discrete dLMs that leads to semi-autoregressive token commitment per block.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To overcome these limitations, we present <span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Nemotron-Labs-Sigma</span> (3B/8B): <span id="S1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">s</span>cal<span id="S1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">i</span>ng up <span id="S1.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">G</span>aussian diffusion <span id="S1.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">m</span>odels for l<span id="S1.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">a</span>nguage. For brevity, we refer to the model family simply as <span id="S1.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> throughout the remainder of the paper. We propose a family of continuous dLMs operating over a 16-dimensional embedding space trained blockwise via likelihood optimization. Within each block, the model learns to jointly denoise Gaussian-corrupted token embeddings and to structure an optimal embedding geometry. To scale training, we warm-start the model from existing pretrained AR weights. For inference, we explore diffusion trajectory sampling, identifying embedding-space Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) and Score Temperature (ST) as crucial ingredients for high-fidelity reasoning and coding.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">

</div></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.13" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S1.F1.14" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> <span id="S1.F1.14.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Left: Inference pipeline.</span> <span id="S1.F1.14.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> generates text blockwise via iterative diffusion denoising over 16D continuous latents (<math id="S1.F1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>) conditioned on a KV-cached prefix (<math id="S1.F1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}</annotation></semantics></math>), followed by categorical readout. Predicted vocabulary probabilities <math id="S1.F1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\theta}(\mathbf{z}_{t},t;\mathbf{c})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\theta}(\mathbf{z}_{t},t;\mathbf{c})</annotation></semantics></math> map to mean predictions <math id="S1.F1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{e}_{\theta}(\mathbf{z}_{t},t;\mathbf{c})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{e}_{\theta}(\mathbf{z}_{t},t;\mathbf{c})</annotation></semantics></math> in 16D space via categorical reparameterization. Clean embeddings (dots) lie on the 16D unit sphere, while <math id="S1.F1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{e}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{e}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> lies on or within it. <span id="S1.F1.14.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Middle: Smooth trajectory enables low-NFE reasoning.</span> GSM8K accuracy vs. NFEs using DDIM sampler for <span id="S1.F1.14.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> ​​(-<span id="S1.F1.14.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unreg</span>)-8B, and sampler <a href="#A6.E17" title="In F.1 Method and Training Objective ‣ Appendix F Implementation Details and Additional Results for Few-step Distillation ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a> for <span id="S1.F1.14.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="S1.F1.14.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">distill</span>-8B. <span id="S1.F1.14.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Right: Scaling inference-time compute.</span> pass@<math id="S1.F1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="S1.F1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> on MBPP (solid curves: fixed config across <math id="S1.F1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>; thin curves: alternative tested configs). </span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Our key contributions are summarized as follows:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">First Large-Scale Continuous dLM:</span> We present <span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Nemotron-Labs-Sigma</span> (3B/8B), efficiently trained by warm-starting from pretrained AR weights, and optimizing a regularized continuous diffusion ELBO.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Competitive Math &amp; Coding:</span> Across six base and ten instruct benchmarks, <span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> outperforms state-of-the-art discrete dLMs/ARs on reasoning and coding.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Inference Steering (CFG &amp; ST):</span> By elucidating the inference design space, we show that embedding-space CFG and ST effectively govern the quality-diversity trade-off with minimal latency overhead via single-pass block-causal attention packing.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Distillation:</span> We study trajectory- and distribution-matching distillation (DMD) methods and find that phased DMD delivers the strongest acceleration, speeding up inference by <math id="S1.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="8\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8\times</annotation></semantics></math> for math and <math id="S1.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times</annotation></semantics></math> for coding, reaching the equivalent of 8 and 4 tokens per forward (TPFs), respectively.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Speculative Decoding:</span> We apply speculative decoding to both distilled and non-distilled <span id="S1.I1.i5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> variants, and find that combining distillation with one-step speculative decoding is highly effective, yielding a <math id="S1.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\sim\!3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∼</mo><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim\!3\times</annotation></semantics></math> throughput improvement over AR on an NVIDIA GB200 GPU.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Background</h2>

<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Notation.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> be a sequence of length <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> over a vocabulary <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math> of size <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math>. We identify <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> with a matrix in <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0,1\}^{L\times V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0,1\}^{L\times V}</annotation></semantics></math> whose rows <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}^{1},...,{\mathbf{x}}^{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>L</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}^{1},...,{\mathbf{x}}^{L}</annotation></semantics></math> are one-hot vectors in <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>V</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{V}</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta^{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>V</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta^{V}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the probability simplex over <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the inner product. NELBO stands for negative evidence lower bound.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Plaid.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Continuous dLMs lift discrete tokens into a low-dimensional Euclidean space and run Gaussian diffusion. There have been multiple proposed design choices, see <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Related Work ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">App.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> for an overview.
We adopt the embedding and diffusion process from Plaid <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gulrajani and Hashimoto, 2023</a>)</cite>, a Variational Diffusion Model (VDM, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kingma et al. (2021)</a></cite>) over token embeddings.
Let <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{E}}\in\mathbb{R}^{V\times d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐄</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{E}}\in\mathbb{R}^{V\times d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math> be a learnable embedding matrix whose rows lie on the unit sphere, with <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{e}\ll V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>≪</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{e}\ll V</annotation></semantics></math>.
The embedding of <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> is given by <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}:={\mathbf{x}}{\mathbf{E}}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐞</mi><mo>:=</mo><mi>𝐱𝐄</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}:={\mathbf{x}}{\mathbf{E}}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math> (i.e., standard embedding lookup). The forward process applies variance-preserving Gaussian noise on <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{SNR}(t)=\alpha_{t}^{2}/\sigma_{t}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>SNR</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>/</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{SNR}(t)=\alpha_{t}^{2}/\sigma_{t}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> decreasing monotonically over <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. A denoiser <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t)\in(\Delta^{V})^{L}\subset\mathbb{R}^{L\times V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>V</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>L</mi></msup><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t)\in(\Delta^{V})^{L}\subset\mathbb{R}^{L\times V}</annotation></semantics></math> with output prior returns a categorical distribution over the vocabulary at every position. The reverse process is the exact Gaussian posterior <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q({\mathbf{z}}_{s}\mid{\mathbf{z}}_{t},{\mathbf{x}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q({\mathbf{z}}_{s}\mid{\mathbf{z}}_{t},{\mathbf{x}})</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kingma et al., 2021</a>, App. A.2)</cite> with <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> replaced by <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t)</annotation></semantics></math>. Its NELBO splits into 3 terms: prior KL <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{prior}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>prior</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{prior}}</annotation></semantics></math>, reconstruction loss <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{rec}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>rec</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{rec}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and diffusion loss <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{diff}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>diff</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{diff}}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Learned noise schedule.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The schedule admits
<math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma(t)=\gamma_{0}+(\gamma_{1}-\gamma_{0})\tilde{\gamma}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>γ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma(t)=\gamma_{0}+(\gamma_{1}-\gamma_{0})\tilde{\gamma}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> with learnable endpoints
<math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{0}&lt;\gamma_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{0}&lt;\gamma_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and a monotone interior shape <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\gamma}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>γ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\gamma}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, giving
<math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{t}^{2}=\sigma(-\gamma(t))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{t}^{2}=\sigma(-\gamma(t))</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}^{2}=\sigma(\gamma(t))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}^{2}=\sigma(\gamma(t))</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{SNR}(t)={\mathrm{e}}^{-\gamma(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>SNR</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{SNR}(t)={\mathrm{e}}^{-\gamma(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>.<span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            <math id="footnote1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(t)=1/(1+{\mathrm{e}}^{-t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(t)=1/(1+{\mathrm{e}}^{-t})</annotation></semantics></math> is the sigmoid function.</span></span></span> The diffusion term depends on the endpoints alone and is invariant to <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\gamma}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>γ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\gamma}(t)</annotation></semantics></math>, which instead controls its Monte-Carlo (MC) variance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kingma et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, so
they are learned for different reasons. Learning the interior-shape distributes denoising difficulty over <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Learned embeddings.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The
NELBO <a href="#S2.E2" title="In Plaid. ‣ 2 Background ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> depends on <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{E}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐄</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{E}}</annotation></semantics></math> via <a href="#S2.E1" title="In Plaid. ‣ 2 Background ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, where embeddings become likelihood-trained parameters, which separates Plaid from continuous dLMs built on fixed (e.g., one-hot)
encodings. Not learning embeddings significantly worsens Plaid’s performance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Self-conditioning (SC).</h5>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Proposed in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al. (2023)</a></cite>, SC lets the denoiser see its own previous estimate. Let <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t;{\mathbf{e}}_{\text{sc}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mtext>sc</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t;{\mathbf{e}}_{\text{sc}})</annotation></semantics></math> denote a denoiser taking an additional predicted clean embedding <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}_{\text{sc}}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mtext>sc</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}_{\text{sc}}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>𝟎</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> for the empty condition (omitted by default in our notation). During training, <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25\%</annotation></semantics></math> of training samples are self-conditioned: a first pass without gradient tracking produces <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}_{\text{sc}}:={\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t;{\mathbf{0}}){\mathbf{E}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mtext>sc</mtext></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>𝟎</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐄</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}_{\text{sc}}:={\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t;{\mathbf{0}}){\mathbf{E}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and only the second pass, <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t;\operatorname{sg}({\mathbf{e}}_{\text{sc}})){\mathbf{E}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>sg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mtext>sc</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐄</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t;\operatorname{sg}({\mathbf{e}}_{\text{sc}})){\mathbf{E}}</annotation></semantics></math>, receives gradients. The remaining samples use <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>𝟎</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> as SC input, so the denoiser learns both branches. During validation, all samples enable SC. Since <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}_{\text{sc}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mtext>sc</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}_{\text{sc}}</annotation></semantics></math> is itself a function of <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">({\mathbf{z}}_{t},t)</annotation></semantics></math>, the NELBO remains valid. Notice that during training, <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25\%</annotation></semantics></math> SC increases the non-embedding FLOPs by only about <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8\%</annotation></semantics></math>, which is minimal. Furthermore, during inference, one directly feeds the previous-step’s prediction as SC, which incurs no overhead.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scaling.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">RePlaid <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2026</a>)</cite> realigns Plaid with the architectures of modern
discrete dLMs/ARs and finds that, once aligned, continuous diffusion scales competitively with masked diffusion.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models</h2>

<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F2.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="S3.F2.sf1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> Training procedure of <span id="S3.F2.sf1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">

</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S3.F2.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> <span id="S3.F2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Training procedure of <span id="S3.F2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> (a) and its transformer attention mask (b)</span> for an example sequence <math id="S3.F2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> of length <math id="S3.F2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=6</annotation></semantics></math> with block size <math id="S3.F2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}=2</annotation></semantics></math>.
During pretraining, we feed the clean discrete tokens <math id="S3.F2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}</annotation></semantics></math> to the AR stream (a, left part) and the noisy continuous embeddings <math id="S3.F2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}</annotation></semantics></math> to the diffusion stream (a, right part).
For the diffusion stream, each block is randomly chosen to either compute the reconstruction loss (1st block, <math id="S3.F2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0</annotation></semantics></math>) or the diffusion loss (2nd &amp; 3rd blocks, <math id="S3.F2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Unif</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>); see <a href="#S3.E5" title="In Training. ‣ 3.1 Blockwise Probabilistic Model ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.
Reconstruction loss is the cross entropy between the logits and the ground truth tokens, while for diffusion loss we use categorical reparameterization to obtain the mean embedding prediction and compute the mean squared error against the ground truth diffusion embeddings.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Blockwise Probabilistic Model</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Inspired by Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion (NLD, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al. (2026)</a></cite>), a state-of-the-art open-sourced masked dLM, we adopt a blockwise formulation for our continuous diffusion language model: the sequence <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> is partitioned into <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> contiguous blocks <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}\}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b}=1}^{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>B</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}\}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b}=1}^{B}</annotation></semantics></math> of size <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}=L/B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}=L/B</annotation></semantics></math>, where the model denoises one block at a time given its clean prefix. As in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Arriola et al. (2025)</a></cite>, we factorize the likelihood autoregressively <em id="S3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">across</em> blocks and then bound each factor:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle-\log p_{\theta}({\mathbf{x}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle-\log p_{\theta}({\mathbf{x}})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E3.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle={\textstyle\sum}_{b=1}^{B}-\log p_{\theta}({\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}\mid{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}&lt;b})})\leq{\textstyle\sum}_{b=1}^{B}\mathcal{L}_{\text{NELBO}}({\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})};{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}&lt;b})})=:\mathcal{L}_{\text{BD}}({\mathbf{x}})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mi>log</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo <section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The reconstruction loss at <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0</annotation></semantics></math> and diffusion loss at <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> do not share a single forward pass. RePlaid evaluates one of them per <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}</annotation></semantics></math> via Horvitz–Thompson estimator <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Horvitz and Thompson, 1952</a>)</cite> with <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R\sim\mathrm{Ber}(p_{\text{rec}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Ber</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>rec</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R\sim\mathrm{Ber}(p_{\text{rec}})</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>rec</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">&lt;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>rec</mtext></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>diff</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">&lt;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{NELBO}}({\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})};{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}&lt;b})})=\E_{R\sim\mathrm{Ber}(p_{\text{rec}})}\big[\mathcal{L}_{\text{prior}}({\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})})+\tfrac{R}{p_{\text{rec}}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{rec}}({\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})};{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}&lt;b})})+\tfrac{1-R}{1-p_{\text{rec}}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{diff}}({\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})};{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}&lt;b})})\big].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Notice that this is an unbiased estimator if <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{diff}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>diff</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{diff}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{rec}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>rec</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{rec}}</annotation></semantics></math> are unbiased. We set <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\text{rec}}=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>rec</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\text{rec}}=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>, empirically found to minimize the training objective variance of RePlaid.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To construct the unbiased estimator for <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{BD}}({\mathbf{x}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>BD</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{BD}}({\mathbf{x}})</annotation></semantics></math> in <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3.1 Blockwise Probabilistic Model ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> for training, we sample <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}</annotation></semantics></math> i.i.d. for each block. If <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}=0</annotation></semantics></math>, we sample <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{z}}_{t^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐳</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{z}}_{t^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}</annotation></semantics></math>; otherwise, we set <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0</annotation></semantics></math> and sample <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{z}}_{0}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐳</mi><mn>0</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{z}}_{0}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}</annotation></semantics></math>. The noise schedule endpoints are learned to optimize <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{NELBO}}({\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})};{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}&lt;b})})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>NELBO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">&lt;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{NELBO}}({\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})};{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}&lt;b})})</annotation></semantics></math> while the schedule interior shape is learned to optimize its MC variance, with both shared across blocks. As mentioned before, we apply SC only to <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25\%</annotation></semantics></math> of samples (full sequence with all blocks). See <a href="#alg1" title="In Appendix B Training and Inference Algorithms ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Alg.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> for the training algorithm.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Pretraining</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">NLD utilizes AR initialization and regularization to enhance downstream performance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. However, adapting these techniques to continuous dLMs like <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> is non-trivial, as the activation dynamics of continuous and discrete models differ fundamentally; it is thus unclear whether discrete AR initialization remains as effective for continuous representation space. To establish a rigorous baseline, we first align <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>’s data, architecture, and optimization with discrete dLMs for a controlled comparison at scale (<a href="#S3.SS2.SSS1" title="3.2.1 Unified Pretraining of Continuous and Discrete dLMs ‣ 3.2 Pretraining ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2.1</span></a>). In <a href="#S3.SS2.SSS2" title="3.2.2 AR Initialization and Regularization ‣ 3.2 Pretraining ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2.2</span></a>, we evaluate the impact of AR initialization when pretraining <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unreg</span>-3B<span id="footnote2" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">2</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            “<span id="footnote2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unreg</span>” means no regularization loss for the diffusion embedding <math id="footnote2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{E}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐄</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{E}}</annotation></semantics></math>. This additional loss will be introduced in <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Embedding Regularization ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>.</span></span></span>
with <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3.1 Blockwise Probabilistic Model ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, followed by an investigation of AR regularization for training our flagship 3B/8B models.</p>
</div>

Proper AR initialization/regularization leads to the best <span id="S3.F3.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> model.
