<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.4" class="ltx_p">The multiplier <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> compensates for the <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/V</annotation></semantics></math> scaling of the expected squared characteristic-function discrepancy under i.i.d. uniform embeddings.
We add <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{susreg}}s({\mathbf{E}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>susreg</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐄</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{susreg}}s({\mathbf{E}})</annotation></semantics></math> per token on the diffusion arm, contributing <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{diff}}\lambda_{\text{susreg}}s({\mathbf{E}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>diff</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>susreg</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐄</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{diff}}\lambda_{\text{susreg}}s({\mathbf{E}})</annotation></semantics></math> to the joint objective (<a href="#alg1" title="In Appendix B Training and Inference Algorithms ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Alg.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). Plain SUSReg-3B/8B uses <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{susreg}}=0.005" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>susreg</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.005</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{susreg}}=0.005</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=512</annotation></semantics></math> freshly sampled directions, and <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P=17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P=17</annotation></semantics></math> trapezoidal points over <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-5,5]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-5,5]</annotation></semantics></math>. The target characteristic function is cached using 512-point numerical quadrature. The <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(VM(d_{e}+P))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(VM(d_{e}+P))</annotation></semantics></math> cost is negligible relative to the transformer.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.02665v2/mollweide_100k_150k_comparison.png" id="A3.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/178;" width="381" height="178" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F10.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="A3.F10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> Density plot of a random <math id="A3.F10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{S}^{15}\to\mathbb{S}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mn>15</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{S}^{15}\to\mathbb{S}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> Mollweide projection of all learned embeddings living on <math id="A3.F10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{S}^{15}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mn>15</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{S}^{15}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The baseline collapses to a small subregion of the 16D space, while SUSReg distributes density more evently, but still contains many concentrated clusters. MS-SUSReg achieves a comparatively much more uniform distribution. Note that while the MS-SUSReg cloud looks uniform in density, it is far from simple random initialization, see the conceptual hierarchical clustering shown in <a href="#A3.F11" title="In Sketched Uniform Spherical Regularization (SUSReg). ‣ C.1 Learning Regularized Embeddings ‣ Appendix C Implementation Details and Additional Results for Pretraining ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>.
The PCA effective dimensions of three embedding matrices at 150k steps are <math id="A3.F10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.4008,15.9593,15.9986" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.4008</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>15.9593</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>15.9986</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.4008,15.9593,15.9986</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A3.F11" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.02665v2/susreg_mssusreg_clustering_dendrogram.svg" id="A3.F11.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/254;" width="476" height="254"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F11.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 11</span>: </span><span id="A3.F11.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Dendrogram on a set of single-token example words, constructed by bottom-up average-linkage clustering of the selected unit-normalized embedding rows in the 3B model variants (Unregularized baseline, SUSReg, MS-SUSReg), using Euclidean distances, with the cluster merge distance shown on the y-axis. </figure>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multiscale-SUSReg (MS-SUSReg).</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The SUSReg regularizer <a href="#A3.E7" title="In Sketched Uniform Spherical Regularization (SUSReg). ‣ C.1 Learning Regularized Embeddings ‣ Appendix C Implementation Details and Additional Results for Pretraining ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> contains the Gaussian kernel <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\mathrm{e}}^{-t^{2}/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathrm{e}}^{-t^{2}/2}</annotation></semantics></math>, which corresponds to a specific low-pass weighting of the frequencies in the compared characteristic functions. This means the loss is more sensitive to larger-scale structural mismatches (global uniformity) than to the finer scales (local clustering). We generalize this by introducing a kernel width parameter <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>

</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the second form is from a simple change of variables with <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u=t/\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u=t/\beta</annotation></semantics></math>. The original SUSReg loss <a href="#A3.E7" title="In Sketched Uniform Spherical Regularization (SUSReg). ‣ C.1 Learning Regularized Embeddings ‣ Appendix C Implementation Details and Additional Results for Pretraining ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> corresponds to <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=1</annotation></semantics></math>. To regularize both the global and the local structure, we can then sum <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> loss terms like <a href="#A3.E8" title="In Multiscale-SUSReg (MS-SUSReg). ‣ C.1 Learning Regularized Embeddings ‣ Appendix C Implementation Details and Additional Results for Pretraining ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> with different weights <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and kernel widths <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A3.EGx12" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>

<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">which we call the <em id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Multiscale-SUSReg</em> (MS-SUSReg) loss. Its scale weights <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> are absolute coefficients: the per-token objective contains <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{diff}}s_{\mathrm{MS}}({\mathbf{E}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>diff</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>MS</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐄</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{diff}}s_{\mathrm{MS}}({\mathbf{E}})</annotation></semantics></math>, without an additional SUSReg multiplier.
Each bandwidth uses <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{k}=1+\lceil\beta_{k}(P-1)\rceil" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌉</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{k}=1+\lceil\beta_{k}(P-1)\rceil</annotation></semantics></math> quadrature points to preserve frequency resolution: 17 and 257 points for <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math>. The scales share <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=512</annotation></semantics></math> random directions and embedding projections, use <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\max}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\max}=5</annotation></semantics></math>, and are active from step zero. Cached targets give a total cost of <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(VM(d_{e}+\sum_{k}P_{k}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(VM(d_{e}+\sum_{k}P_{k}))</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Local repulsion regularization.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">MS-SUSReg encourages distributional uniformity through sampled projections, but does not explicitly enforce separation between individual embedding pairs. Nearly coincident embeddings can therefore remain difficult to distinguish under diffusion noise. To address this directly, we add a local separation penalty related to maximum hyperspherical separation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib86" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. Namely, we add a per-token weighted loss term <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{diff}}\lambda_{\mathrm{rep}}s_{\mathrm{rep}}({\mathbf{E}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>diff</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>rep</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>rep</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐄</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{diff}}\lambda_{\mathrm{rep}}s_{\mathrm{rep}}({\mathbf{E}})</annotation></semantics></math>, where</p>
<table id="A3.EGx13" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.E11"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle s_{\mathrm{rep}}({\mathbf{E}}):=\frac{1}{2V}\sum_{u&lt;v}\max\{0,r-\|{\mathbf{e}}_{u}-{\mathbf{e}}_{v}\|_{2}\}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>rep</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐄</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle s_{\mathrm{rep}}({\mathbf{E}}):=\frac{1}{2V}\sum_{u&lt;v}\max\{0,r-\|{\mathbf{e}}_{u}-{\mathbf{e}}_{v}\|_{2}\}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">penalizes pairwise chord distances below an exclusion radius <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>. We set <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\max\{\sqrt{2(1-c)},2\Phi^{-1}(1-p){\mathrm{e}}^{\gamma_{0}/2}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\max\{\sqrt{2(1-c)},2\Phi^{-1}(1-p){\mathrm{e}}^{\gamma_{0}/2}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi</annotation></semantics></math> is the standard normal CDF, and <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=0.9995" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9995</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=0.9995</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.01</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.01</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\mathrm{rep}}=20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>rep</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\mathrm{rep}}=20</annotation></semantics></math>.
Unlike maximum hyperspherical separation, which maximizes the smallest pairwise distance, our penalty acts on all pairs within <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>.
The adaptive term depending on <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> defines a target separation corresponding to a per-competitor confusion probability of <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> under the diffusion forward marginal distribution at the minimum noise level <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>. We disable gradients through <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> here so this loss only affects the embeddings and not <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We evaluate all unordered pairs in tiles across data-parallel workers without storing the full pairwise matrix. Both embedding regularizers act from step zero, including on SC-selected sequences, and are excluded from reported NELBO/perplexity.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Riemannian Adam step.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since the effective embeddings have unit norm, their geometry depends only on their directions. The naive embedding representation, which normalizes each unconstrained row on the fly when used, creates a per-row dependence of the effective learning rate on arbitrary underlying pre-normalization row norms. We find that these row norms grow over training, resulting in an uncontrolled LR decay on the embedding rows. With the following Riemannian Adam step, we optimize the embedding rows directly on the sphere to make every update respect the on-sphere constraint and avoid this uncontrolled influence on the embedding LR. For each row <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>, we project its total training-loss gradient <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{g}_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{g}_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> onto the tangent space at <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{g}_{v}^{\perp}=\mathbf{g}_{v}-\langle\mathbf{g}_{v},{\mathbf{e}}_{v}\rangle{\mathbf{e}}_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐠</mi><mi>v</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐠</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{g}_{v}^{\perp}=\mathbf{g}_{v}-\langle\mathbf{g}_{v},{\mathbf{e}}_{v}\rangle{\mathbf{e}}_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>. Similar to <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib85" title="" class="ltx_ref">Becigneul and Ganea (2019)</a></cite>, we adapt the step size separately for each embedding vector. We apply a bias-corrected on-manifold Adam variant using a tangent first moment and one scalar second moment per row, estimated from <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{g}_{v}^{\perp}\|_{2}^{2}/d_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐠</mi><mi>v</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{g}_{v}^{\perp}\|_{2}^{2}/d_{e}</annotation></semantics></math>. This scalar second moment rescales all tangent directions equally. After the update, we project the row back onto the sphere by normalization and parallel-transport the first moment along the shortest spherical geodesic to the new tangent space, preserving momentum as the embedding direction changes.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Projected noise-schedule updates.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our main regularized model (<span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-3B/8B) uses a degree-32 Bernstein polynomial for the noise schedule shape with increments <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi_{i}\geq 10^{-3}/32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi_{i}\geq 10^{-3}/32</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{i}\psi_{i}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{i}\psi_{i}=1</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Initializing <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi_{i}=1/32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi_{i}=1/32</annotation></semantics></math> gives a linear schedule. Adam updates on the variance objective are projected onto this simplex; endpoint AdamW updates use weight decay <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math> and enforce <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{1}-\gamma_{0}\geq 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>≥</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{1}-\gamma_{0}\geq 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>. All three groups use Adam coefficients <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta_{1},\beta_{2})=(0.9,0.95)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.95</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta_{1},\beta_{2})=(0.9,0.95)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon=10^{-8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon=10^{-8}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training details for the regularized models.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For the plain SUSReg ablation models (Sigma -preg-3B/8B):<span id="footnote3" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup>
                  <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note"><span id="footnote3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright">3</span></span>
                  
                  
                  
                  
                  
                  
                  
                <span id="footnote3.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright">“</span><span id="footnote3.11" class="ltx_text">preg</span><span id="footnote3.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright">” stands for plain SUSReg.</span></span></span></span></span>
we add the described SUSReg loss in <a href="#A3.E7" title="In Sketched Uniform Spherical Regularization (SUSReg). ‣ C.1 Learning Regularized Embeddings ‣ Appendix C Implementation Details and Additional Results for Pretraining ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> and freeze the embeddings and schedule parameters after 100k steps, but otherwise follow the original model’s training recipe including the change to <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{diff}}=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>diff</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{diff}}=0.3</annotation></semantics></math> at 100k steps.
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For MS-SUSReg (Sigma-3B/8B):</span> we use <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta_{1},w_{1})=(1,10^{-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta_{1},w_{1})=(1,10^{-2})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta_{2},w_{2})=(16,10^{-4})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta_{2},w_{2})=(16,10^{-4})</annotation></semantics></math>, and repulsion weight <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\mathrm{rep}}=20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>rep</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\mathrm{rep}}=20</annotation></semantics></math>. The embedding uses Riemannian Adam; the schedule uses the projected updates above. Their learning rates warm up to <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> over 1.5k steps, decay by cosine to <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> at 30k, remain constant through 120k, then follow WSD decay to <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math> at 150k. Embeddings and schedules remain trainable throughout, with <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{diff}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>diff</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{diff}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Global gradient-norm clipping is 3 for 3B and 1 for 8B.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Full pretrained results for all three variants.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A3.T6" title="In Full pretrained results for all three variants. ‣ C.1 Learning Regularized Embeddings ‣ Appendix C Implementation Details and Additional Results for Pretraining ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> reports the six generative reasoning tasks of <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tabs.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> for all three pretrained variants at both scales. In diffusion mode, plain SUSReg is roughly neutral against <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unreg</span> at DDPM-256 but gains <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.40</annotation></semantics></math> (3B) and <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.79" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.79</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.79</annotation></semantics></math> (8B) average points at DDIM-32, consistent with our hypothesis that uniform embeddings mainly buy robustness to coarse discretization; MS-SUSReg improves on both at every operating point and scale.</p>

<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Ablation Study: MDLM Initialization for Pretraining</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">[Back to <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Pretraining ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> in the main paper.]</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">All <span id="A3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> models featured in our main results are warm-started from an AR checkpoint (“AR initialization” in <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) and then trained for <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="300" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>300</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">300</annotation></semantics></math>B tokens under the joint diffusion + AR objective (<a href="#S3.SS2.SSS2" title="3.2.2 AR Initialization and Regularization ‣ 3.2 Pretraining ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2.2</span></a>). We ablate that choice against a masked diffusion language model (MDLM) warm start: identical <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="300" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>300</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">300</annotation></semantics></math>B-token recipe, run instead from the released Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-3B checkpoint of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al. (2026)</a></cite>, which is our main baseline in <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. All other knobs are held fixed.</p>
</div>

models at the two CFG–ST configurations of <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, both with SC enabled: DDPM (<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math> steps, EDM <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=7</annotation></semantics></math> schedule, <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w=2" display="inline" alttext="\tau=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>) and DDIM (<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=0.3</annotation></semantics></math>). Numbers are mean <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> two standard errors over <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> sampling lanes, forming a <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> confidence interval of the mean.</p>

<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Results.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">MDLM initialization has a small but consistent win on average at both configurations, but the sign of the change is task-dependent rather than uniform. MBPP and MBPP+ strongly favor MDLM initialization, while HumanEval and HumanEval+ show opposite trends.</p>

<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Benchmarks.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate on ARC-e/c <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib67" title="" class="ltx_ref">Clark et al., 2018</a>)</cite>, HellaSwag <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zellers et al., 2019</a>)</cite>, PIQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib69" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bisk et al., 2020</a>)</cite>, WinoGrande <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib70" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sakaguchi et al., 2020</a>)</cite>, and MMLU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib71" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hendrycks et al., 2021</a>)</cite>.
These benchmarks score a candidate response <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐫</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math> against a prompt <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐩</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> by comparing <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log p_{\theta}({\mathbf{r}}\mid{\mathbf{p}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐫</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>𝐩</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log p_{\theta}({\mathbf{r}}\mid{\mathbf{p}})</annotation></semantics></math> across candidates.
Per Open LLM Leaderboard convention, we report the plain likelihood on WinoGrande and MMLU, and the likelihood normalized by character length on the other four tasks which are length-varying.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scoring our continuous method.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> does not give likelihood in closed form, but a surrogate based on the NELBO: taking the prompt as the clean prefix and the candidate as the block to be denoised, and then applying <a href="#S3.Ex2" title="In 3.1 Blockwise Probabilistic Model ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> verbatim with <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐩</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}&lt;b})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">&lt;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}&lt;b})}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐫</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐱</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}b})}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scoring the masked baseline via count-based NELBO.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first give a brief introduction of masked diffusion models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sahoo et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shi et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ou et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. There, the latent <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{z}}_{t}\in\mathcal{V}^{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>L</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{z}}_{t}\in\mathcal{V}^{L}</annotation></semantics></math> is a partially masked token sequence: each position is independently kept clean with probability <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-t</annotation></semantics></math> or replaced by the mask token <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{m}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐦</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{m}}</annotation></semantics></math> with probability <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. The denoiser <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t})\in(\Delta^{V})^{L}\subset\mathbb{R}^{L\times V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>V</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>L</mi></msup><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{t})\in(\Delta^{V})^{L}\subset\mathbb{R}^{L\times V}</annotation></semantics></math> returns a categorical distribution over clean tokens at each position; one can prove that it needs not to take time argument as <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> carries no information about <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> beyond what <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{z}}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{z}}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> already reveals <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ou et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. The resulting NELBO is a <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{t}</annotation></semantics></math>-weighted cross entropy over the masked positions only.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐩</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> be the prompt and <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐫</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math> be a candidate response. We generate the masked states by the <em id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">mask set</em>, instead of randomly masking each position with probability <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>: for <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\subseteq\{1,\dots,L_{\mathbf{r}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>𝐫</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\subseteq\{1,\dots,L_{\mathbf{r}}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\mathbf{r}}:=|{\mathbf{r}}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>𝐫</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝐫</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{\mathbf{r}}:=|{\mathbf{r}}|</annotation></semantics></math>, we obtain <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{z}}_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{z}}_{M}</annotation></semantics></math> from masking indices in <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐫</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and denote
<math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="C(M):=\sum_{l\in M}-\log\langle{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}^{l}({\mathbf{z}}_{M};{\mathbf{p}}),\,{\mathbf{r}}^{l}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">:=</mo><msub><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mi>log</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>θ</mi><mi>l</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><mi>𝐩</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msup><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(M):=\sum_{l\in M}-\log\langle{\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}^{l}({\mathbf{z}}_{M};{\mathbf{p}}),\,{\mathbf{r}}^{l}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> their cross entropy. Conditioning that bound on <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐩</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> and integrating <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> out yields an average over
the <em id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">number</em> of masked tokens <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ou et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nie et al., 2025</a>)</cite>:</p>

<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\binom{[L_{\mathbf{r}}]}{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>𝐫</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\binom{[L_{\mathbf{r}}]}{n}</annotation></semantics></math> means the set of all <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-element subsets of <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[L_{\mathbf{r}}]:=\{1,2,...,L_{\mathbf{r}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>𝐫</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>𝐫</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[L_{\mathbf{r}}]:=\{1,2,...,L_{\mathbf{r}}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. <a href="#A4.E14" title="In Scoring the masked baseline via count-based NELBO. ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details and Additional Results for Likelihood-based Benchmarks ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> is a Rao–Blackwellized low-variance estimator of <a href="#A4.E13" title="In Scoring the masked baseline via count-based NELBO. ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details and Additional Results for Likelihood-based Benchmarks ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>, manifested in the following three major differences: <em id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(i)</em> The <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{t}</annotation></semantics></math> weight becomes <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{L_{\mathbf{r}}}{n}\leq L_{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>𝐫</mi></msub><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>𝐫</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{L_{\mathbf{r}}}{n}\leq L_{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math>, so rare small-<math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> draws that leave one or two masked tokens would not cause the variance of the estimator to blow up. <em id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(ii)</em> Bernoulli masking leaves <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐫</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math> wholly unmasked with
probability <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1-t)^{L_{\mathbf{r}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>𝐫</mi></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1-t)^{L_{\mathbf{r}}}</annotation></semantics></math>, which may be common for short responses and wastes a forward pass, while the <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> constraint avoids this. <em id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.2.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(iii)</em> As <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> is finite, we can similarly use stratified sampling as the <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-grid above, spreading counts evenly
over <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,\ldots,L_{\mathbf{r}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>𝐫</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,\ldots,L_{\mathbf{r}}\}</annotation></semantics></math> from one uniform offset, so every batch covers all masking rates.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In practice, we use <a href="#A4.E14" title="In Scoring the masked baseline via count-based NELBO. ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details and Additional Results for Likelihood-based Benchmarks ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> with <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> low-discrepancy draws <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and standard random sampling for <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> for Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2026</a>)</cite> in <a href="#A4.T8" title="In Appendix D Implementation Details and Additional Results for Likelihood-based Benchmarks ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tabs.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> and <a href="#A4.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details and Additional Results for Likelihood-based Benchmarks ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>. On MMLU candidates are
single tokens, so
<math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\mathbf{r}}=n=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>𝐫</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{\mathbf{r}}=n=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <a href="#A4.E14" title="In Scoring the masked baseline via count-based NELBO. ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details and Additional Results for Likelihood-based Benchmarks ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> is exact after one forward pass, while
<a href="#A4.E13" title="In Scoring the masked baseline via count-based NELBO. ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details and Additional Results for Likelihood-based Benchmarks ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> would still be averaging <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. We found <a href="#A4.E14" title="In Scoring the masked baseline via count-based NELBO. ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details and Additional Results for Likelihood-based Benchmarks ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> to work better than <a href="#A4.E13" title="In Scoring the masked baseline via count-based NELBO. ‣ Appendix D Implementation Details and Additional Results for Likelihood-based Benchmarks ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> in early experiments.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Length generalization.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Diffusion training denoises blocks of exactly <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>
tokens from packed sequences of length <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>, whereas candidates are
typically short and occasionally longer than <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>. For each <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="({\mathbf{p}},{\mathbf{r}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐩</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">({\mathbf{p}},{\mathbf{r}})</annotation></semantics></math> pair, we apply causal attention over <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐩</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> and bidirectional attention over <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐫</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math>, assuming that the bidirectional attention can generalize to response length other than <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>. The attention map follows the conditional branch in <a href="#S4.F5.sf1" title="In Figure 5 ‣ Score temperature (ST). ‣ 4.2 Trajectory Steering ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5(a)</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>

<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Sampler Updates</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1=t_{0}&gt;\cdots&gt;t_{N}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">&gt;</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.1389em">⋯</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em">&gt;</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1=t_{0}&gt;\cdots&gt;t_{N}=0</annotation></semantics></math>, with
<math id="A5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{i}=\alpha_{t_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{i}=\alpha_{t_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{i}=\sigma_{t_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{i}=\sigma_{t_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A5.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{i}=\sigma_{i}/\alpha_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{i}=\sigma_{i}/\alpha_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, and
<math id="A5.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\lambda_{i}=\log(\alpha_{i}/\sigma_{i})=-\gamma(t_{i})/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>log</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mi>γ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{i}=\log(\alpha_{i}/\sigma_{i})=-\gamma(t_{i})/2</annotation></semantics></math>.
At step <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, the clean prediction
<math id="A5.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{i}={\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{i},t_{i};{\mathbf{c}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐞</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{i}={\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{z}}_{i},t_{i};{\mathbf{c}})</annotation></semantics></math> implies
<math id="A5.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\bm{\epsilon}}_{i}=({\mathbf{z}}_{i}-\alpha_{i}\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{i})/\sigma_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold-italic" mathvariant="bold-italic">ϵ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐞</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\bm{\epsilon}}_{i}=({\mathbf{z}}_{i}-\alpha_{i}\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{i})/\sigma_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Predictions incorporate CFG and ST as in <a href="#S4.Ex4" title="In Classifier-free guidance (CFG). ‣ 4.2 Trajectory Steering ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">CFG</span></a> and <a href="#S4.Ex5" title="Equation ST ‣ Score temperature (ST). ‣ 4.2 Trajectory Steering ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">ST</span></a>.</p>
</div>

<p id="A5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">[Back to <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 ODE Sampler and Time Discretization ‣ 5 Few-Step Generation ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a> in the main paper.]</p>

</span></figcaption>
