<div id="A5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We mainly consider the following discretization schemes. Let <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> be the total number of steps and assume the <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th step (<math id="A5.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1,...,N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1,...,N</annotation></semantics></math>) goes from <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i-1}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}&lt;t_{i-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}&lt;t_{i-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
<ul id="A5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Learned: arithmetic progression in time: <math id="A5.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}=1-\frac{i}{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>i</mi><mi>N</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}=1-\frac{i}{N}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Uniform-<math id="A5.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>: arithmetic progression in <math id="A5.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, the minus log-SNR: <math id="A5.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma(t_{i})=\gamma_{\max}+\frac{i}{N}(\gamma_{\min}-\gamma_{\max})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>i</mi><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma(t_{i})=\gamma_{\max}+\frac{i}{N}(\gamma_{\min}-\gamma_{\max})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">EDM <math id="A5.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2022</a>)</cite>: first convert the VP schedule to VE by defining <math id="A5.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}_{t}:=\frac{\sigma_{t}}{\alpha_{t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}_{t}:=\frac{\sigma_{t}}{\alpha_{t}}</annotation></semantics></math> as the essential standard deviation at time <math id="A5.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. The grid points are chosen so that <math id="A5.I1.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}_{t_{i}}^{1/\rho}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}_{t_{i}}^{1/\rho}</annotation></semantics></math> is an arithmetic progression, i.e., <math id="A5.I1.i3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}_{t_{i}}=\left(\tilde{\sigma}_{\max}^{1/\rho}+\frac{i}{N}(\tilde{\sigma}_{\min}^{1/\rho}-\tilde{\sigma}_{\max}^{1/\rho})\right)^{\rho}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>max</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>i</mi><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>min</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>max</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>ρ</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}_{t_{i}}=\left(\tilde{\sigma}_{\max}^{1/\rho}+\frac{i}{N}(\tilde{\sigma}_{\min}^{1/\rho}-\tilde{\sigma}_{\max}^{1/\rho})\right)^{\rho}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Note that as <math id="A5.I1.i3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, this converges to the uniform-<math id="A5.I1.i3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> scheme.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A5.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">We visualize the three schemes in <a href="#A5.F13" title="In E.2 Ablation Study: Time Discretization ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>. Empirically, we find that for high NFE sampling, both the uniform-<math id="A5.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> and EDM <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=7</annotation></semantics></math> schemes perform similarly, while uniform-<math id="A5.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> generally performs the best for low NFE sampling. See <a href="#A5.F14" title="In E.2 Ablation Study: Time Discretization ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> for the few-step reasoning accuracy of DDPM and DDIM over GSM8K and HumanEval.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.3 </span>Reasoning and Coding Benchmark Setup</h3>

<div id="A5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">[Back to <a href="#S4" title="4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Secs.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#S5" title="5 Few-Step Generation ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> in the main paper.]</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We describe the harness, scoring pipeline, and sampler that produce <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tabs.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, <a href="#A5.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> and <a href="#A5.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>. The scoring pipeline is consistent for all base models and generation modes.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Benchmarks and few-shot budgets.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use six tasks from <span id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">lm-evaluation-harness</span> following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al. (2026)</a></cite>:
GSM8K (8-shot, 1319 questions) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cobbe et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, Minerva Math (4-shot, 5000 questions<span id="footnote4" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">4</span>
                
                
                
                
                
                
                
              Number of questions in each sub-domain: algebra 1187, counting/prob 474, geometry 479, intermediate algebra 903, number theory 540, prealgebra 871, precalc 546.</span></span></span>) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib72" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lewkowycz et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, HumanEval and HumanEval+ (0-shot, 164 questions) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib73" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, and MBPP and MBPP+ (3-shot, 500 and 378 questions, respectively) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib74" title="" class="ltx_ref">Austin et al., 2021</a>)</cite>.
The per-task generation budget is 256 tokens for GSM8K and 512 tokens for the other five tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scoring.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GSM8K is scored by exact-match on the numerical answer, extracted from the model’s response by a permissive regex that keeps the last number appearing in the completion (stripping separators and trailing punctuation).
Minerva Math is scored by symbolic equivalence after canonicalizing boxed and inline expressions.
HumanEval and HumanEval+ report post-processed pass@<math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>: the completion is stripped out of the Markdown code fence, an AST-based longest-valid-code extraction is applied, and the resulting program is executed against the task test cases in the container.
MBPP and MBPP+ report the harness pass@<math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> directly without this post-processing step, matching the convention of prior work.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Decoding configuration.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All <span id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> diffusion-mode runs use block size <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}=32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}=32</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">BF16</span> model weights at inference time, and operation of SC follows <a href="#S4.F5.sf2" title="In Figure 5 ‣ Score temperature (ST). ‣ 4.2 Trajectory Steering ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5(b)</span></a>. The DDPM-256 row uses the ancestral sampler of <a href="#A5.E15" title="In DDPM. ‣ E.1 Sampler Updates ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> on the EDM <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=7</annotation></semantics></math> time discretization (<a href="#A5.SS2" title="E.2 Ablation Study: Time Discretization ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.2</span></a>); the DDIM-32 row uses the deterministic sampler of <a href="#A5.E16" title="In DDIM. ‣ E.1 Sampler Updates ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> on the uniform-<math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> time discretization.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Seed error bars.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each <span id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> diffusion row aggregates <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> independent sampling lanes as follows. For question <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, we independently draw <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> responses under the same model with <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> different seeds. Let <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i,j}</annotation></semantics></math> be the score of the <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>-th response to question <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. We first average over questions to obtain <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> per-lane scores <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{j}=\operatorname{mean}_{i}(s_{i,j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>mean</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{j}=\operatorname{mean}_{i}(s_{i,j})</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=1,\dots,10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j=1,\dots,10</annotation></semantics></math>, and then obtain <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{s}=\operatorname{mean}_{j}(s_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>mean</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{s}=\operatorname{mean}_{j}(s_{j})</annotation></semantics></math> together with the across-lane standard deviation <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\sigma}=\operatorname{std}_{j}(s_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>std</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\sigma}=\operatorname{std}_{j}(s_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>. The half-widths in <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> are <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{2}{\sqrt{10}}\hat{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>10</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{\sqrt{10}}\hat{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math>, an approximate <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> confidence interval for the mean.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Baseline decoders.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The AR-mode for NLD and <span id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> row uses greedy argmax at each step; NLD’s diffusion-mode row uses the confidence-threshold greedy sampler of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al. (2026)</a></cite> (block size <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}=32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}=32</annotation></semantics></math>; <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\argmax" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>argmax</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\argmax</annotation></semantics></math> readout at every position whose top-1 probability exceeds a threshold; we report the better of thresholds <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.9</annotation></semantics></math> per task). For LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B we quote each model’s best diffusion-mode number without the confidence-threshold rule: at each denoising step the single position with the highest top-1 confidence is unmasked.
Both rules are instances of confidence-based decoding <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chang et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, and both inherit the absorbing property of masked diffusion: once a position is unmasked, its token is frozen for the rest of the trajectory.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.4 </span>Sweeping Classifier-Free Guidance and Score Temperature</h3>

<div id="A5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">[Back to <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Trajectory Steering ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> or <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a> in the main paper.]</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In <a href="#A5.F15" title="In E.4 Sweeping Classifier-Free Guidance and Score Temperature ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figs.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> and <a href="#A5.F16" title="Figure 16 ‣ E.4 Sweeping Classifier-Free Guidance and Score Temperature ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a>, we present the full tables for CFG and ST sweep for our <span id="A5.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A5.SS4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unreg</span>-3B models trained with and without AR regularization, respectively.</p>
</div>

<section id="A5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.5 </span>Ablation Study: Auto-Guidance with Self-Conditioning</h3>

<div id="A5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">[Back to <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Trajectory Steering ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> in the main paper.]</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Standard CFG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ho and Salimans, 2022</a>)</cite>, also following the idea of auto-guidance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib62" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karras et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, extrapolates a conditional prediction away from a “bad” prediction to sharpen the model’s prediction. Self-conditioning introduces a second source of conditioning, as is used in existing continuous dLMs (e.g., <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al. (2026)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Potaptchik et al. (2026)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al. (2026)</a></cite>; see <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Related Work ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">App.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> for detailed discussion).
We define the following notations in this subsection:</p>

<p id="A5.SS5.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where the good prediction <math id="A5.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}^{+}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}^{+}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> is the conditional prediction that uses both the clean context and SC; for either bad prediction <math id="A5.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}^{-}_{\theta}\in\{{\mathbf{e}}^{{\mathbf{c}},{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta},{\mathbf{e}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mrow><mi>𝐜</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}^{-}_{\theta}\in\{{\mathbf{e}}^{{\mathbf{c}},{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta},{\mathbf{e}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, the guided mean embedding prediction is</p>
<table id="A5.EGx18" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A5.Ex11"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS5.p2.3" class="ltx_p">The <span id="A5.SS5.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">context-preserving</span> baseline keeps the prompt and previously generated blocks in both branches and sets <math id="A5.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}^{-}_{\theta}\leftarrow{\mathbf{e}}^{{\mathbf{c}},{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mrow><mi>𝐜</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}^{-}_{\theta}\leftarrow{\mathbf{e}}^{{\mathbf{c}},{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>; it therefore extrapolates only away from the prediction made without SC.
Our proposed method in <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Trajectory Steering ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> instead uses the fully unconditional branch <math id="A5.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}^{-}_{\theta}\leftarrow{\mathbf{e}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}^{-}_{\theta}\leftarrow{\mathbf{e}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, removing both clean context and SC.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Experimental setup.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare the two choices using the same <span id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unreg</span>-3B checkpoint with block length <math id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>, full GSM8K and HumanEval evaluation sets, and 10 samples per problem. The DDIM sweep uses <math id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> steps per block, uniform-<math id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> schedule, and ST <math id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=0.3</annotation></semantics></math>; the DDPM sweep uses <math id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math> steps per block, EDM <math id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=7</annotation></semantics></math> schedule, and ST <math id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=1</annotation></semantics></math>. We remark that the guidance is inactive at <math id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w=1</annotation></semantics></math> and the two choices coincide.</p>
</div>

<section id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Results.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in <a href="#A5.T12" title="In Experimental setup. ‣ E.5 Ablation Study: Auto-Guidance with Self-Conditioning ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tabs.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> and <a href="#A5.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ Experimental setup. ‣ E.5 Ablation Study: Auto-Guidance with Self-Conditioning ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>, the fully unconditional bad prediction (ours) is consistently stronger in the useful guidance range:
it almost wins every matched CFG weight in sweep on both tasks and both samplers, and, tuned over the sweep, reaches a higher ceiling in each task.
Thus, we conclude that the advantage shown here is not an artifact of using different guidance search ranges.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.6 </span>Ablation Study: Steering in Logit Space instead of Embedding Space</h3>

<div id="A5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">[Back to <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Trajectory Steering ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> in the main paper.]</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Both steering knobs introduced in <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Trajectory Steering ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> act on the predicted clean embedding <math id="A5.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{L^{\prime}\times d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{L^{\prime}\times d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math>, equivalently on the score or velocity. Recall that our denoiser leverages <span id="A5.SS6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">categorical reparameterization</span>, i.e., <math id="A5.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}=\operatorname{softmax}({\bm{\ell}}_{\theta}){\mathbf{E}}={\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}{\mathbf{E}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ℓ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐄</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐄</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}=\operatorname{softmax}({\bm{\ell}}_{\theta}){\mathbf{E}}={\mathbf{x}}_{\theta}{\mathbf{E}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A5.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bm{\ell}}_{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{L^{\prime}\times V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ℓ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bm{\ell}}_{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{L^{\prime}\times V}</annotation></semantics></math> are the predicted logits, and <math id="A5.SS6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{softmax}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>softmax</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{softmax}</annotation></semantics></math> operates in the vocabulary dimension. Thus, a natural alternative is to apply the same operations to <math id="A5.SS6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bm{\ell}}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ℓ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bm{\ell}}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> before the <math id="A5.SS6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{softmax}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>softmax</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{softmax}</annotation></semantics></math>. This is the form of guidance used by discrete dLMs, which does not have embedding-space prediction to steer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nie et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib63" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Schiff et al., 2025</a>)</cite> (<a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Related Work ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">App.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Logit-space CFG (LCFG).</h5>

<div id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Reusing the notations in <a href="#A5.SS5" title="E.5 Ablation Study: Auto-Guidance with Self-Conditioning ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.5</span></a>, with the same fully unconditional bad prediction, we do softmax on the extrapolated logits:</p>
<table id="A5.EGx19" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A5.Ex12"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle{\mathbf{e}}^{w,\text{logit}}_{\theta}:=\operatorname{softmax}({\bm{\ell}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}+w\,[{\bm{\ell}}^{+}_{\theta}-{\bm{\ell}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}]){\mathbf{E}},\qquad w\geq 1," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>logit</mtext></mrow></msubsup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ℓ</mi><mi>θ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0.170em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ℓ</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ℓ</mi><mi>θ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐄</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle{\mathbf{e}}^{w,\text{logit}}_{\theta}:=\operatorname{softmax}({\bm{\ell}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}+w\,[{\bm{\ell}}^{+}_{\theta}-{\bm{\ell}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}]){\mathbf{E}},\qquad w\geq 1,</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">against our default <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}^{w}_{\theta}={\mathbf{e}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}+w[{\mathbf{e}}^{+}_{\theta}-{\mathbf{e}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mi>w</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}^{w}_{\theta}={\mathbf{e}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}+w[{\mathbf{e}}^{+}_{\theta}-{\mathbf{e}}^{\varnothing,{\mathbf{0}}}_{\theta}]</annotation></semantics></math> of <a href="#S4.Ex4" title="In Classifier-free guidance (CFG). ‣ 4.2 Trajectory Steering ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">CFG</span></a>, which extrapolates after the softmax. The two coincide at <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w=1</annotation></semantics></math> (i.e., no guidance).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Logit temperature (LT).</h5>

<div id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This is the analogue of ST in logit space, which rescales the conditional logits themselves:</p>
<table id="A5.EGx20" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A5.Ex13"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle{\mathbf{e}}^{T}_{\theta}:=\operatorname{softmax}\Big(\frac{{\bm{\ell}}^{+}_{\theta}}{T}\Big){\mathbf{E}},\qquad T\in[0,1]," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msubsup><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ℓ</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mi>T</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐄</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle{\mathbf{e}}^{T}_{\theta}:=\operatorname{softmax}\Big(\frac{{\bm{\ell}}^{+}_{\theta}}{T}\Big){\mathbf{E}},\qquad T\in[0,1],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=1</annotation></semantics></math> recovers the conditional mean embedding prediction (i.e., no guidance), and smaller <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> sharpens. The <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> limit is the maximum a posteriori (MAP) denoiser <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{e}}^{0}_{\theta}={\mathbf{E}}[\argmax{\bm{\ell}}^{+}_{\theta}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐄</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">argmax</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ℓ</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{e}}^{0}_{\theta}={\mathbf{E}}[\argmax{\bm{\ell}}^{+}_{\theta}]</annotation></semantics></math>, which snaps the prediction onto a single vocabulary embedding.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We remark that both operations change the trajectory only; tokens are still read out as the <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\argmax" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>argmax</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\argmax</annotation></semantics></math> of the conditional logits at the final step <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0</annotation></semantics></math>, exactly as in <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Block Diffusion Sampling ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Secs.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> and <a href="#alg2" title="Algorithm 2 ‣ Appendix B Training and Inference Algorithms ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. Also, LCFG does not cost extra compute compared with the embedding-space counterpart, since we need to get both conditional and unconditional logit predictions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Experimental setup.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the setting identical to the default in <a href="#A5.SS5" title="E.5 Ablation Study: Auto-Guidance with Self-Conditioning ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.5</span></a>. We use the same <span id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unreg</span>-3B checkpoint with block length <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>, the full GSM8K and HumanEval evaluation sets, and generate 10 responses per problem. DDIM uses <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> steps/block on a uniform-<math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> time discretization with <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=0.3</annotation></semantics></math>, and DDPM uses <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math> steps/block on the EDM <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=7</annotation></semantics></math> time discretization and <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>

<section id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Results.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Logit-space CFG (LCFG) peaks at <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w=2</annotation></semantics></math> in all four settings, whereas embedding-space CFG improves up to <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w=4\sim 10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>∼</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w=4\sim 10</annotation></semantics></math>; at their respective optima, LCFG gains only <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.30</annotation></semantics></math> points on GSM8K/DDIM and loses <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.44\sim 17.26" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.44</mn><mo>∼</mo><mn>17.26</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.44\sim 17.26</annotation></semantics></math> points elsewhere (<a href="#A5.T14" title="In Experimental setup. ‣ E.6 Ablation Study: Steering in Logit Space instead of Embedding Space ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>). Logit temperature (LT) provides effective sharpening without a second branch: on DDPM, lowering <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/5</annotation></semantics></math> raises GSM8K from <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="52.44" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>52.44</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">52.44</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="79.11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>79.11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">79.11</annotation></semantics></math>, while the MAP endpoint <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=0</annotation></semantics></math> retains <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78.61" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>78.61</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78.61</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#A5.T15" title="In Experimental setup. ‣ E.6 Ablation Study: Steering in Logit Space instead of Embedding Space ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>). Relative to matched sharpening (<math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=1/w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=1/w</annotation></semantics></math>), the unconditional branch in LCFG contributes negligibly at <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w=2</annotation></semantics></math> and hurts at larger weights. LT also complements ST, adding <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9.42</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.42</annotation></semantics></math> points on DDIM with ST <math id="A5.SS6.SSS0.Px4.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=0.3</annotation></semantics></math>, but reduces accuracy when combined with both CFG and ST (<a href="#A5.T16" title="In Experimental setup. ‣ E.6 Ablation Study: Steering in Logit Space instead of Embedding Space ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a>). We therefore retain embedding-space CFG and ST as the default choice.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.7 </span>Ablation Study: Commit-Stride Sampling</h3>

<div id="A5.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">[Back to <a href="#S4" title="4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> in the main paper.]</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond blockwise decoding of <math id="A5.SS7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens per denoising window, we further introduce a <em id="A5.SS7.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">commit stride</em> <math id="A5.SS7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\in\{1,\dots,L^{\prime}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\in\{1,\dots,L^{\prime}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Each denoising window still runs the same blockwise reverse process over a block of fresh Gaussian noise with length <math id="A5.SS7.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}=32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}=32</annotation></semantics></math>, but only the leading <math id="A5.SS7.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\in\{8,16,32\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\in\{8,16,32\}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens are committed back into the causal KV cache; the remaining <math id="A5.SS7.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}-S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}-S</annotation></semantics></math> tail positions are discarded and re-drawn as fresh noise in the next window (which is shifted forward by <math id="A5.SS7.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> absolute positions). Setting <math id="A5.SS7.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\leftarrow L^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\leftarrow L^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> recovers the default block-decoding method.
The pseudocode for commit stride can be found in <a href="#alg2" title="In Appendix B Training and Inference Algorithms ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Alg.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.
This is a pure inference-time technique that further improves the output quality even under matched compute budgets, as we will see below.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Setup.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate on the base models of <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tabs.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>: <span id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unreg</span>-3B/8B, both with block size <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}=32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}=32</annotation></semantics></math>. Decoding invariants match the diffusion-mode rows of <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.4 Mathematical Reasoning and Coding Performance ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. For each stride, CFG <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math> and ST <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> are chosen based on the number of DDIM steps per window (<a href="#A5.T10" title="In Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>): <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w,\tau)=(3,0.2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w,\tau)=(3,0.2)</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 64</annotation></semantics></math> steps, <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(3,0.3)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3,0.3)</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" All cells generate <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> samples for each prompt and report mean <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> two standard errors (<a href="#A5.SS3" title="E.3 Reasoning and Coding Benchmark Setup ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.3</span></a>).</p>

<section id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Nominal vs. true NFE.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For simplicity, we match compute cost by <em id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">nominal</em> NFE, defined as the number of denoiser forward passes required to commit <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}=32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}=32</annotation></semantics></math> tokens under the given (steps, stride) pair:</p>
<table id="A5.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Nominal\penalty\ NFE}\;:=\;\frac{NL^{\prime}}{S}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>Nominal NFE</mtext><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">:=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mi>S</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Nominal\penalty\ NFE}\;:=\;\frac{NL^{\prime}}{S},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of diffusion steps per denoising window.
Since every denoising window operates on the <em id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">same</em> <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>-wide noisy block appended to the same-length clean prefix, one forward pass costs the same FLOPs regardless of <math id="A5.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>

NFE</em> is the nominal number of forward passes per <math id="A5.T17.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> committed tokens (i.e., <math id="A5.T17.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{steps}/\text{stride}\times 32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>steps</mtext><mo>/</mo><mtext>stride</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{steps}/\text{stride}\times 32</annotation></semantics></math>).
