<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Implementation Details and Additional Results for Supervised Fine-Tuning</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">[Back to <a href="#S7" title="7 Supervised Fine-Tuning ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> in the main paper.]</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.1 </span>Supervised Fine-Tuning Setup</h3>

<div id="A7.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our SFT pipeline uses NeMo-RL with joint diffusion and AR supervision on assistant responses, following Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion (NLD) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. Prompts remain clean, and training and evaluation share the non-thinking chat boundary described below.
We freeze the diffusion embedding <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{E}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐄</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{E}}</annotation></semantics></math>, noise-schedule network <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\gamma}_{\psi}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>γ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>ψ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\gamma}_{\psi}(t)</annotation></semantics></math>, and endpoints <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{0},\gamma_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{0},\gamma_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>. The clean-stream input embedding, transformer, conditioning projections, and both readout heads remain trainable. Therefore, SUSReg is used only during pretraining.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Initialization and objective.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We initialize from the 150k-step pretrained <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unreg</span>-3B/8B, <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">preg</span>-3B/8B, and <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-3B/8B checkpoints.
Before SFT of <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">preg</span>-8B and <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-8B, we reinitialize the AR embedding rows with <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> norm below <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math> to the mean direction of the remaining rows, scaled to their median norm. This includes chat-boundary IDs 10 and 11 and prevents the initial gradient-norm transient caused by their near-zero embeddings. The repair is applied once; its benchmark effect is not separately ablated.
Let <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the supervised answer positions, including the terminal EOS padding described below. The SFT objective is</p>
<table id="A7.EGx25" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A7.E39"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A7.E39.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{sft}}=\alpha\,\frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{A}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{BD},i}}{|\mathcal{A}|}+\frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{A}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{ar},i}}{|\mathcal{A}|}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>sft</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mtext>BD</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mtext>ar</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{sft}}=\alpha\,\frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{A}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{BD},i}}{|\mathcal{A}|}+\frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{A}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{ar},i}}{|\mathcal{A}|},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(39)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{BD}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>BD</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{BD}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the continuous block NELBO of <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3.1 Blockwise Probabilistic Model ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and <a href="#S3.Ex2" title="In 3.1 Blockwise Probabilistic Model ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, including its diffusion, reconstruction, and prior terms, and <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{ar}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>ar</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{ar}}</annotation></semantics></math> is next-token cross-entropy from the clean stream <a href="#S3.E6" title="In AR Regularization. ‣ 3.2.2 AR Initialization and Regularization ‣ 3.2 Pretraining ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>. The ELBO weight is <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.3</annotation></semantics></math> for <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unreg</span>-3B/8B and <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">preg</span>-3B/8B, and <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=1</annotation></semantics></math> for <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-3B/8B, following pretraining (<a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Implementation Details and Additional Results for Pretraining ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">App.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>). Numerators and token counts are reduced globally across data-parallel ranks. The AR and diffusion denominators coincide under the answer mask because position zero is unsupervised, so <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> has the same meaning as the pretraining diffusion-loss weight.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As in pretraining (<a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Pretraining ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>), we estimate the reconstruction and diffusion terms with the Horvitz–Thompson estimator in <a href="#S3.E5" title="In Training. ‣ 3.1 Blockwise Probabilistic Model ‣ 3 Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>: independently for each block, we select reconstruction at <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0</annotation></semantics></math> with probability <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathrm{rec}}=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>rec</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathrm{rec}}=0.1</annotation></semantics></math> and otherwise draw <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Unif</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. Gaussian noise is applied only in embedding space; the token IDs always remain clean. Prompt and ordinary batch-padding positions have zero loss and are pinned to their clean embeddings, whereas the synthetic EOS padding is supervised. Answer blocks see the clean context <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{c}}=({\mathbf{p}},{\mathbf{r}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}&lt;b})})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐜</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐩</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>𝐫</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">&lt;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#006E37;" mathcolor="#006E37">b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{c}}=({\mathbf{p}},{\mathbf{r}}^{({\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.2148}&lt;b})})</annotation></semantics></math> of <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Block Diffusion Sampling ‣ 4 Language Generation via Continuous Diffusion Sampling ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Data and preprocessing.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the same non-thinking, single-turn SFT corpus as NLD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib78" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chandiramani et al., 2026</a>)</cite>: <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="848{,}087" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>848,087</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">848{,}087</annotation></semantics></math> training and <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}200</annotation></semantics></math> validation conversations, each with an empty system message, a user prompt, and an assistant response.
We use the same Mistral-NeMo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib66" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mistral AI, 2024</a>)</cite> tokenizer (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V=131{,}072" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>131,072</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V=131{,}072</annotation></semantics></math>) and the Nemotron Nano chat template <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib79" title="" class="ltx_ref">Blakeman et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, explicitly setting <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">enable_thinking=false</span>. Thus, the supervised response follows the intended prompt suffix <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;think&gt;&lt;/think&gt;</span>; training and evaluation use the same answer boundary.
During training, we left-pad prompts with at most <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="31" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>31</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">31</annotation></semantics></math> unsupervised tokens so answers begin on the <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>-token block grid; no padding is inserted between prompt and answer. Inference uses unpadded, fully causal prompts. Supervised EOS tokens complete the final answer block, with one full EOS block appended when already aligned. Unsupervised right-padding then rounds the batch length to a multiple of <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1024</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1024</annotation></semantics></math> to limit FlexAttention compilation shapes. Samples exceeding <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8192</annotation></semantics></math> tokens after padding are dropped.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Optimization.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both model sizes train for <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8000</annotation></semantics></math> steps (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx 2.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 2.4</annotation></semantics></math> epochs) at sequence length and maximum position <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8192</annotation></semantics></math>, block length <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>, and global/micro batch sizes <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256/1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>256</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256/1</annotation></semantics></math>. We use AdamW with <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta_{1},\beta_{2})=(0.9,0.98)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.98</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta_{1},\beta_{2})=(0.9,0.98)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon=10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon=10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>, weight decay <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math>, and learning rate <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.5\times 10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.5\times 10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math> after <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math> steps of linear warmup, held constant thereafter. Training uses <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">BF16</span>, gradient clipping at <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math>, and FSDP2 with TP<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{}={}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>=</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}={}</annotation></semantics></math>CP<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{}={}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>=</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}={}</annotation></semantics></math>1, activation checkpointing, and no sequence packing. Self-conditioning is enabled for <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25\%</annotation></semantics></math> of microbatches on every optimizer step and all validation sequences. The chat template enables the generation prompt; clean-prompt, answer-only supervision and EOS padding follow the preprocessing above.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Setting the maximum position to <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8192</annotation></semantics></math> also extends the pretrained rotary frequencies: the effective YaRN factor is <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8192/16384=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>8192</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>16384</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8192/16384=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, compared with <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.25</annotation></semantics></math> at the pretraining length of <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4096</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4096</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.2 </span>Evaluation Setup, CFG–ST Sweep, and Full Results</h3>

<div id="A7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The instruct evaluations in <a href="#S7.T4" title="In Results. ‣ 7 Supervised Fine-Tuning ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tabs.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#S7.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Results. ‣ 7 Supervised Fine-Tuning ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> use the base-model harness (<a href="#A5.SS3" title="E.3 Reasoning and Coding Benchmark Setup ‣ Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.3</span></a>), with the differences below.</p>

<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Benchmarks.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate GSM8K (1319 problems), MATH-500 (500), AIME 2024/2025 (30 each), HumanEval+ (164), MBPP (378), LiveCodeBench-CPP (454), MMLU (14042), GPQA (198), and IFEval (541), using the SFT chat template and diffusion block length <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}=32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}=32</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scoring.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Math tasks use symbolic equivalence on the final <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">\boxed{}</span> answer; GSM8K also accepts the last number. HumanEval and MBPP report executed pass@<math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> on EvalPlus’s base tests (<span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">passing_base_tests</span>), and LiveCodeBench-CPP compiles and tests extracted C++ programs. GPQA and MMLU request reasoning ending in <span id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Answer: \boxed{A/B/C/D}</span>; grading extracts the last boxed letter, with a regex fallback. IFEval reports instruction-level loose accuracy, matching the reference models in <a href="#S7.T4" title="In Results. ‣ 7 Supervised Fine-Tuning ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tabs.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#S7.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Results. ‣ 7 Supervised Fine-Tuning ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Baselines.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Baseline scores come from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al. (2026, Tabs. 5, 7)</a></cite>, except NLD-8B diffusion, which we reproduce under the aligned protocol without format injection. We use SDAR-8B Chat at TPF <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=1.00" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>1.00</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=1.00</annotation></semantics></math> rather than <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.75</annotation></semantics></math>: it scores higher on eight tasks, with gaps <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 0.6</annotation></semantics></math> points on the remaining two (MMLU and HumanEval).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Decoding algorithms.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As in the evaluation for base models, we always enable SC; DDPM-256 uses EDM <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=7</annotation></semantics></math> schedule, and DDIM-32 uses uniform-<math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> schedule. Their respective <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w,\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w,\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> settings follow the recommended values for base models <a href="#A5.T10" title="In Appendix E Implementation Details and Additional Results for Inference ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Generation budget.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The generation budget is <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1024</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1024</annotation></semantics></math> tokens for GSM8K and HumanEval at 3B, rising to <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1536" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1536</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1536</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2560" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2560</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2560</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively, at 8B; <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2560" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2560</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2560</annotation></semantics></math> for MBPP, LiveCodeBench-CPP, and IFEval; and <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4096</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4096</annotation></semantics></math> for AIME 2024/2025, MATH-500, and GPQA. MMLU uses <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2048</annotation></semantics></math> for 3B DDPM and <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2560" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2560</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2560</annotation></semantics></math> otherwise. AR uses <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16384" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16384</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16384</annotation></semantics></math> except on MMLU (<math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2560" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2560</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2560</annotation></semantics></math>). Caps follow per-lane graded-answer lengths: no correct answer in the smoke runs required more than <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4096</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4096</annotation></semantics></math> tokens, and the longer tail consists mainly of degenerate repetition.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Seed error bars.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each diffusion row averages <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> independent sampling lanes and reports half-width <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{2}{\sqrt{10}}\hat{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>10</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{\sqrt{10}}\hat{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> is the standard deviation of per-lane benchmark scores. AR greedily decodes the clean stream through its AR head.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Post-SFT CFG–ST sweep.</h5>

<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On GSM8K and HumanEval, the pre-SFT guidance and temperature optima remain within sampling uncertainty of the best post-SFT settings for both 3B checkpoints and samplers (<a href="#A7.T20" title="In Post-SFT CFG–ST sweep. ‣ G.2 Evaluation Setup, CFG–ST Sweep, and Full Results ‣ Appendix G Implementation Details and Additional Results for Supervised Fine-Tuning ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a>). The 8B SUSReg checkpoint uses the corresponding 3B settings without a separate sweep.</p>
</div>

<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Implementation Details and Additional Results for Self-Speculative Decoding</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section gives the protocol (<a href="#A8.SS1" title="H.1 Setup ‣ Appendix H Implementation Details and Additional Results for Self-Speculative Decoding ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H.1</span></a>) and all results:
the models of <a href="#S6" title="6 Self-Speculative Decoding ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> in full (<a href="#A8.SS2" title="H.2 Main Results in Full ‣ Appendix H Implementation Details and Additional Results for Self-Speculative Decoding ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H.2</span></a>),
the undistilled <span id="A8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> with trained drafters (<a href="#A8.SS3" title="H.3 Undistilled Model and Trained Drafters ‣ Appendix H Implementation Details and Additional Results for Self-Speculative Decoding ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H.3</span></a>),
and acceptance training (<a href="#A8.SS4" title="H.4 Acceptance Training of the Distilled Model ‣ Appendix H Implementation Details and Additional Results for Self-Speculative Decoding ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H.4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.1 </span>Setup</h3>

<section id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Drafting and verification.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following the two-pass framework of NLD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2026</a>, Sec. 3.3)</cite>, each round initializes one block of <math id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}=32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}=32</annotation></semantics></math> draft positions with Gaussian noise in the 16-dimensional latent space and reads out categorical draft tokens from a single denoiser call at <math id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1</annotation></semantics></math>.
The AR head then scores all drafts causally in one forward pass over the shared backbone and cached prefix, keeps the longest prefix that matches its own greedy tokens, and appends one token of its own.
Draft-only parameters are disabled during verification, so the committed text is the model’s greedy AR output, up to <span id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">BF16</span> near-ties between the decoding and verification kernels.
More denoiser calls per draft raised AL but not tokens per forward pass, so we use one.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Trained drafters.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Optionally, we train draft-only parameters on Tulu-3 prompts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib90" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lambert et al., 2024</a>)</cite> with NLD’s LK-hybrid and verifier cross-entropy objective <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2026</a>, Eqs. 6–9)</cite>, keeping the backbone and the AR head frozen.
We train a rank-128 LoRA on the query and value projections together with the diffusion head (<em id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Q/V</em>, 440M parameters at 3B and 595M at 8B).
At 8B, the 6 of 1,000 training steps whose gradient norm is not finite make no update.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Benchmarks.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GSM8K (1,319 problems, 8-shot chain of thought), HumanEval (164), and MBPP (500) use the prompts of our base-model evaluation.
The end-of-text token is ignored, and an answer ends at the first of the task’s stop strings, within 256, 512, and 512 new tokens.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Serving.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We serve with SGLang <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib77" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2024</a>)</cite> in <span id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">BF16</span>, with greedy decoding, TP1, and one request at a time on one NVIDIA GB200.
AL and accuracy use the numerics of the training code (FP32 diffusion-stream parameters and eager kernels).
Throughput uses FlashAttention-4 and CUDA graphs.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">NLD reference.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">NLD-3B-Base and NLD-8B-Base ship without a drafter adapter, so they draft with their own diffusion head.
Every NLD model runs at its released block size: 32 positions holding the last committed token and 31 drafts, one draft fewer per round than <span id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>.
NLD’s speculative server searched only the end of each committed block for stop strings and missed earlier ones; we let it search the whole block, as SGLang’s own speculative path does, so that it stops in the block that contains the first stop.
NLD’s runner times AR and speculative decoding once each, concurrently on two GPUs of one node.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Metrics.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS1.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">AL counts the draft tokens that a round adds to the returned answer, i.e., its committed answer tokens minus the verifier’s own token, pooled over rounds; drafts accepted past the end of the answer are discarded and not counted.
Repetition loops are trivially predictable and would inflate AL.
On GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP, we therefore drop, per model, every prompt whose AR, speculative, or timing output loops (at least half of its 16-grams repeat) or reaches the length cap; accuracy uses all prompts.
Throughput is answer tokens per second of client time, and speedup divides the speculative throughput by the same model’s AR throughput on the same GPU and prompts, averaged over two runs on different GPUs.
Paired gains use the prompts that both models keep, with 95% percentile bootstrap intervals over prompts.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.2 </span>Main Results in Full</h3>

<div id="A8.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A8.T22" title="In H.2 Main Results in Full ‣ Appendix H Implementation Details and Additional Results for Self-Speculative Decoding ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a> lists throughput, speedup, and AL for the models of <a href="#S6" title="6 Self-Speculative Decoding ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, and <a href="#A8.T23" title="In H.2 Main Results in Full ‣ Appendix H Implementation Details and Additional Results for Self-Speculative Decoding ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a> lists their accuracy and kept prompts.
For <span id="A8.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A8.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">distill</span>, a draft–verify round costs 3.0–3.5 AR decoding steps rather than the ideal two.
Speedups are relative to each model’s own AR decoding, which NLD’s serving implementation runs about 20% faster at 3B and 12% faster at 8B.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A8.T22" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A8.T22.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 22</span>: </span><span id="A8.T22.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="A8.T22.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Self-speculative decoding in full.</span>

<section id="A8.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.3 </span>Undistilled Model and Trained Drafters</h3>

<div id="A8.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The undistilled <span id="A8.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-3B and <span id="A8.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-8B can draft with their own diffusion head or with a trained Q/V adapter (<a href="#A8.T24" title="In H.3 Undistilled Model and Trained Drafters ‣ Appendix H Implementation Details and Additional Results for Self-Speculative Decoding ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">24</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Distillation helps more than a trained drafter at 3B.</span>
The adapter raises <span id="A8.SS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-3B’s AL by 13.1%, 5.4%, and 7.2% on GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP ([12.2, 14.0], [3.1, 7.6], and [5.8, 8.9]).
The distilled student, with its own head and no adapter, gains 21.8%, 20.1%, and 15.0% over <span id="A8.SS3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-3B ([20.1, 23.5], [8.6, 31.7], and [11.8, 18.1]).</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">At 8B, the two are closer.</span>
The adapter raises <span id="A8.SS3.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-8B’s AL by 16.1%, 9.4%, and 14.3% ([15.1, 17.1], [6.1, 13.0], and [12.4, 16.1]), and distillation by 22.4%, 7.9%, and 19.9% ([20.9, 24.0], [<math id="A8.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>0.5, 16.8], and [16.7, 23.2]).
Compared directly, <span id="A8.SS3.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A8.SS3.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">distill</span>-8B accepts 5.4% and 4.9% more than <span id="A8.SS3.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-8B with the adapter on GSM8K and MBPP ([4.0, 6.8] and [2.0, 7.7]) and 1.6% fewer on HumanEval ([<math id="A8.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>9.3, 6.4]), where it also decodes slower (2.37<math id="A8.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> against 2.73<math id="A8.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The adapter leaves the output unchanged.</span>
It is disabled during verification, so <span id="A8.SS3.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-3B and <span id="A8.SS3.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span>-8B solve exactly the same problems with and without it.</p>
</div>

<section id="A8.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.4 </span>Acceptance Training of the Distilled Model</h3>

<div id="A8.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Instead of training a separate drafter, we continue the distillation with an acceptance objective that updates the whole backbone; we call the result <span id="A8.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A8.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">distill</span>-<span id="A8.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">spec</span>.
Let <math id="A8.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> denote the parameters of the student, which starts from <span id="A8.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A8.SS4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">distill</span>, and <math id="A8.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> those of a frozen copy of <span id="A8.SS4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A8.SS4.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">distill</span>.
We keep the distillation objective and add two terms.
An LK-hybrid loss aligns the student’s one-call draft with the AR head of <math id="A8.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>, and a KL term holds the student’s AR distribution to that of <math id="A8.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>, so that the verifier, and hence the decoded output, is preserved:</p>
<table id="A8.EGx26" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A8.E40"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

</table>
<p id="A8.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Training updates the shared transformer and the diffusion head; as in distillation (<a href="#A6.SS2" title="F.2 Implementation Details ‣ Appendix F Implementation Details and Additional Results for Few-step Distillation ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.2</span></a>), the embedding matrix <math id="A8.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{E}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐄</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{E}}</annotation></semantics></math>, the noise schedule, and the AR head stay frozen.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Distribution matching.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{DMD}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>DMD</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{DMD}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the student objective of <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Implementation Details and Additional Results for Few-step Distillation ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">App.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a> (<a href="#alg3" title="In F.1 Method and Training Objective ‣ Appendix F Implementation Details and Additional Results for Few-step Distillation ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Alg.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>), with the auxiliary and reference denoisers and the setting of the distillation that produced <span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">distill</span>: two phases, no self-conditioning, and segments that start from fresh student rollouts.
Acceptance training thus continues that distillation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Acceptance.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each LK example takes a context <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{c}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{c}}</annotation></semantics></math> from the generations of an earlier 3B DMD student on math and code prompts, mostly GSM8K- and HumanEval-style, and drafts the next block with one call from pure noise, as in serving (<a href="#A8.SS1" title="H.1 Setup ‣ Appendix H Implementation Details and Additional Results for Self-Speculative Decoding ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H.1</span></a>).
Both sizes use these contexts; the two runs averaged into each <span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">distill</span>-<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">spec</span> model use two versions of the context set.
Test and dev problems are excluded by exact match; a 13-gram scan finds 3, 1, and 54 near-duplicates of GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP test problems among the contexts, and excluding those problems leaves the AL gains of acceptance training unchanged.
Slot <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\in\{1,\ldots,L^{\prime}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\in\{1,\ldots,L^{\prime}\}</annotation></semantics></math> has draft distribution <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{p}^{j}:={\mathbf{x}}^{j}_{\phi}({\mathbf{z}}_{1},1;{\mathbf{c}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>j</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{p}^{j}:={\mathbf{x}}^{j}_{\phi}({\mathbf{z}}_{1},1;{\mathbf{c}})</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{z}}_{1}\sim\mathcal{N}({\mathbf{0}},{\mathbf{I}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟎</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐈</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{z}}_{1}\sim\mathcal{N}({\mathbf{0}},{\mathbf{I}})</annotation></semantics></math> and draft token <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{v}^{j}:=\argmax_{v}\hat{p}^{j}(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msup><mo The verifier reads all slots in one causal pass and gives <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p^{j}:={\mathbf{x}}^{|{\mathbf{c}}|+j}_{\bar{\phi}_{\text{AR}}}(\tilde{\mathbf{x}}^{&lt;|{\mathbf{c}}|+j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext>AR</mtext></msub><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝐜</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝐜</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p^{j}:={\mathbf{x}}^{|{\mathbf{c}}|+j}_{\bar{\phi}_{\text{AR}}}(\tilde{\mathbf{x}}^{&lt;|{\mathbf{c}}|+j})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{c}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{c}}</annotation></semantics></math> followed by the draft tokens.
If the first <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> draft tokens equal the verifier’s greedy tokens <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v^{j}_{\star}:=\argmax_{v}p^{j}(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>v</mi><mo>⋆</mo><mi>j</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.1389em">:=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.167em">argmax</mo><mi>v</mi></msub><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v^{j}_{\star}:=\argmax_{v}p^{j}(v)</annotation></semantics></math> and slot <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a+1</annotation></semantics></math> does not, the loss covers the accepted prefix and the first rejected slot, <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}=\{1,\ldots,\min(a+1,L^{\prime})\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}=\{1,\ldots,\min(a+1,L^{\prime})\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Following NLD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2026</a>, Eqs. 6–9)</cite>, let <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" most probable tokens under <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p^{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><annotation p^{j}(v)^{1/\tau_{\text{LK}}}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v\in U^{j}" display="inline" <td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(41)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega^{j}={\textstyle\sum}_{v\in U^{j}}\min\big(p^{j}_{\tau}(v),\hat{p}^{j}_{\tau}(v)\big)=1-\mathrm{TV}(p^{j}_{\tau},\hat{p}^{j}_{\tau})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ω</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>U</mi><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>τ</mi><mi>j</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>τ</mi><mi>j</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>TV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>τ</mi><mi>j</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>τ</mi><mi>j</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega^{j}={\textstyle\sum}_{v\in U^{j}}\min\big(p^{j}_{\tau}(v),\hat{p}^{j}_{\tau}(v)\big)=1-\mathrm{TV}(p^{j}_{\tau},\hat{p}^{j}_{\tau})</annotation></semantics></math> is the probability that a token sampled from <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{p}^{j}_{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>τ</mi><mi>j</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{p}^{j}_{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> is accepted, and <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>; the weight thus shifts from the KL term toward total variation as the draft approaches the verifier.
The retention term is the forward KL from the AR distribution of <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> to that of the student, averaged over the set <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}</annotation></semantics></math> of the last 128 positions of <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{x}}</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., the <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> draft slots and the 96 context tokens before them:</p>

</section>
<section id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Weights and optimization.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We set <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{LK}}=0.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>LK</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{LK}}=0.25</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{ret}}=12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>ret</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{ret}}=12</annotation></semantics></math>, and cap the retention weight at</p>
<table id="A8.EGx29" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A8.E43"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A8.E43.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\hat{\lambda}_{\text{ret}}=\min\Big(\lambda_{\text{ret}},\;3\,\frac{\|\nabla_{\phi}(\lambda_{\text{DMD}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{DMD}}+\lambda_{\text{LK}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{LK}})\|}{\|\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}_{\text{ret}}\|}\Big)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>ret</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>ret</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 3</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>DMD</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>DMD</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>LK</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>LK</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>ret</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\hat{\lambda}_{\text{ret}}=\min\Big(\lambda_{\text{ret}},\;3\,\frac{\|\nabla_{\phi}(\lambda_{\text{DMD}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{DMD}}+\lambda_{\text{LK}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{LK}})\|}{\|\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}_{\text{ret}}\|}\Big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(43)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with both gradient norms taken from the previous update.
Without the cap, once the AR distribution drifted, the retention gradient grew until it dominated the clipped update, and training diverged.
Each update draws 64 DMD examples and 128 drafts.
The drafts form chains of four rounds: the first round drafts after a prefix of up to 1,664 tokens that keeps the prompt’s BOS token, and each later round drafts after the tokens that the previous round committed, as in serving.
The optimizers are those of <a href="#A6.SS2" title="F.2 Implementation Details ‣ Appendix F Implementation Details and Additional Results for Few-step Distillation ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.2</span></a>, except that the student learning rate is doubled to <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.2\times 10^{-7}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7.2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.2\times 10^{-7}</annotation></semantics></math>; the drafts never use self-conditioning, as in serving.
Each <span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">distill</span>-<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">spec</span> model is a uniform weight average of two runs with <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{DMD}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>DMD</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{DMD}}=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, each trained for 600 updates from <span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sigma</span> -<span id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">distill</span> while the learning rate decays linearly to zero.
At 8B, the teacher-generated DMD data has 16,384 contexts instead of 65,536, and the fit of the query noise levels and the LK contexts are reused from 3B.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Results.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A8.T25" title="In Results. ‣ H.4 Acceptance Training of the Distilled Model ‣ Appendix H Implementation Details and Additional Results for Self-Speculative Decoding ‣ Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">25</span></a> gives the gains.
Acceptance training raises AL by 5.2%, 6.0%, and 6.1% at 3B and by 8.5%, 4.8%, and 8.1% at 8B on GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP; the HumanEval intervals include zero at both sizes.
It leaves AR accuracy unchanged on all three benchmarks at both sizes (sign tests, <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 0.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 0.10</annotation></semantics></math> at 3B and <math id="A8.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 0.69" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.69</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 0.69</annotation></semantics></math> at 8B).</p>
</div>
